style: Read this as the narrator of a premium developer-tool launch film. Confident, warm, crisp and relaxed, with a hint of wry excitement, like a keynote presenter who knows the demo is great. Natural medium pace, clean articulation, no exaggerated inflection, never salesy.

lines.text: This text is made of glass.
Everything you see through it is live video, rendered frame by frame.
Here's what it can do, how it works, and how to ship it at scale.
Chunky, frosted type, with real depth.
A lens that tracks the performer.
Reeded glass, slicing the scene into ribbons.
Frosted panels that react to the music.
Even water, rippling on the beat.
Rain on a window. Every drop, a tiny lens.
And glass that shatters, straight into the next shot.
So how does it work? Three layers.
At the bottom, an E-F video element. Or any HTML at all.
In the middle, E-F surface mirrors those pixels onto a canvas, every single frame.
On top, a WebGL shader samples that canvas, and bends each pixel along the glass's surface normal.
Red, green and blue bend by slightly different amounts. That's the rainbow edge.
One frame task drives it all, on Editframe's clock. So every frame is deterministic.
So the same HTML renders in your browser, from the CLI, or in parallel on the Editframe API.
Glass, at scale. Build it with Editframe.
